findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: probe on the HEAD archive: authorize committed, security recorded, line removed uncommitted -> lens plan run=['correctness','security'], stale.security='(auth) selects lens-security'; never-committed variant -> check_reviews and next both demand security via the record's kinds
findings.message: A moved file's kinds are read from its current text only, so an authorisation call deleted after the security review leaves that record fresh: with `authorize(user)` committed, security recorded, then the line removed, `lens plan` selects security (`why: auth`) but `run` is `['correctness']` and after the correctness re-run `check_reviews` raises no staleness failure for security. The review gate goes green on the removal of the exact control the security lens read, which the digest rule it replaces caught.
findings.minimal_fix: In `_file_kinds` (given base) also match AUTH/ROUTE hints against the removed lines of `git diff <base> -- <rel>`, so plan and staleness agree through the one function.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: flow.py:608 early-returns code only for .md under PROTOCOL_DIRS; _file_kinds('agents/auth.py') on HEAD -> {'auth','code'} (lock test_source_under_agents_is_still_scanned)
findings.message: Every file under `skills/`, `.agents/`, `agents/`, `hooks/` returns `code` before the hint scan, so on HEAD `agents/auth.py` containing `def authorize` yields `['code']` where bdd84c0 yielded `['auth','code',...]`. An adopter whose `agents/` or `hooks/` is a source package loses the security lens on an auth change there; R-9 asks for `code`, not for source under those dirs to go unscanned.
findings.minimal_fix: Early-return `{code}` only when `rel.endswith(".md")`; otherwise add `code` and fall through to the hint scan.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: flow.py:677-681: a moved .aegis/ path returns stale for every lens before the always/triggers logic; the lock test_a_contract_change_re_runs_every_lens (spec edit -> run == lenses, 'contract' in stale.security) passes in the 258-green suite on the archive
findings.message: A change to `.aegis/waivers.json`, `.aegis/answers.json` or the spec after a review re-runs only the always-on lens (their kind is `code`/`docs`), while docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:321 and :364 state that such a change re-takes every review because the review is the control on a waiver. R-9's letter (kinds decide) and §6's stated control conflict, and the code silently drops the control.
findings.minimal_fix: In `lens_staleness`, after computing `moved`, return stale for every lens when any moved path starts with `.aegis/` (contract files), before the always/triggers logic.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: probe on the HEAD archive: removal committed -> plan lenses/run = ['correctness','security'] with why.security=['stale-record'] and check_reviews fails on the same two; after a security re-run both say correctness only; the lock at tests/test_aegis.py:231 commits the removal and fails with the flow.py delta reverted
findings.message: `lens_plan` evaluates staleness only over `selected`, while `check_reviews` and `next` evaluate every recorded lens with the record's stored `kinds`: with `authorize(user)` reviewed by security and the line then removed and committed (or in a never-committed file), `lens plan` prints lenses=['correctness'] and run=['correctness'] while the gate already fails 'security did not review this version', and once correctness re-runs run=[] with the gate still failing and `next` saying 're-run lens-security'. The workflow dispatches `replan.run`, so the refine loop cannot converge; the new lock at tests/test_aegis.py:224 passes only because its removal is uncommitted (diff_text still sees the `-authorize` line).
findings.minimal_fix: In `lens_plan` run the staleness loop over `selected` ∪ recorded lenses (a stale unselected record joins `lenses` and `run`, why `stale-record`) so `run` covers what `check_reviews` fails on; commit the removal in the lock at test_aegis.py:224.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: review_snapshot keys the manifest 'contract:'+sha256(canonical(contract half)) as diff_digest does; a real passing task gate wrote only gate-receipt.json (out of scope) plus status/updated, then a pricing move -> run=['correctness']
findings.message: The task manifest is snapshotted by its full sha while `diff_digest` keys only its contract half, and `_file_kinds` hint-scans its JSON; a `_set_status` bump plus any real move counts the manifest as a moved `code` file whose objective text can carry `session`/`authoriz`. A false re-run of security, only in that conjunction.
findings.minimal_fix: Key `_is_task_manifest` paths by the canonical contract half as `diff_digest` does, and skip the hint scan for `.aegis/` paths.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: the 'unreachable' comment replaced (flow.py:674-676); probe 7: chmod +x -> every lens 'the digest moved after that review (a mode change; no content did)' — the alternative the finding offered
findings.message: The snapshot key omits file mode while `diff_digest` hashes it, so `chmod +x` on a scope file reaches the branch the comment calls unreachable and re-runs every lens. Harmless direction, but the comment is false and a mode change is not scoped by kind.
findings.minimal_fix: Fold `st_mode & 0o777` into the snapshot key (or drop the 'unreachable' comment).
